mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on the source document plus translator certification

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory positive identification of all shareholders, directors, and UBOs against (i) Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) lists, (ii) UN Security Council sanctions consolidated list, (iii) EU consolidated financial sanctions list, (iv) OFAC/SDN list for USD-cleared transactions, and (v) French domestic measures established by Tracfin and other competent authorities; screening must occur before incorporation and at least every six months thereafter, with documented evidence preserved for five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) and Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Article L. 123-1-5 of the Commercial Code and Loi Toubon No. 94-665, the corporate name must be expressed in French or in a form adapted to French usage; the official register accepts only Latin-script names with mandatory French accentuation where applicable; non-Latin script transliteration is required and foreign names must include one French term or an acceptable French transliteration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In the event of a name rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal through the INPI online portal within one month of the refusal notice; the appeal shall state the grounds of objection, submit an alternative clearance certificate, and may include a request for ministerial prior approval for any prohibited token; if the rejection is based on a prior identical or confusingly similar registered name or trademark, the applicant may also seek interim relief before the competent commercial court (Tribunal de commerce) under référé proceedings.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a licensed equity crowdfunding portal under EU Regulation 2020/1503 (ECSP), a virtual office is not permissible as the sole registered office; the AMF and ACPR will require a physical establishment in France with a real presence for compliance personnel, record-keeping, and fit-and-proper assessment. A third-party approved domiciliation service may serve as a registered address for administrative purposes only, but the crowdfunding activity must be effectively managed from an actual French office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High – approximately an 80% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by AMF/ACPR within the first 18 months following final authorization, given the mandatory supervisory cycle for financial intermediaries.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Code de commerce (Book II, Title III): Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 and R.223-1 et seq. governing Société à Responsabilité Limitée; Articles L.123-1 to L.123-12 and L.123-7 et seq. governing registration with the Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS); Regulation (EU) 2020/1503 on European crowdfunding service providers applicable to the licensed business.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce (Commercial Court Registry) through the online National Business Formalities Office operated by INPI (*Guichet des formalités des entreprises*, formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de conformité d'une société and Demande d'immatriculation au Registre du commerce et des sociétés (
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: French law sets no minimum legal capital for a SARL; the share capital is freely determined by the founders. Cash contributions must be deposited in a temporarily blocked bank account or with a notary and cannot be withdrawn until the company is registered with the RCS. For the crowdfunding service provider, after registration the platform must maintain either own funds or professional-indemnity insurance cover satisfying Article 10 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1503.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE BOARD OF MANAGERS OF THE SOCIÉTÉ À RESPONSABILITÉ LIMITÉE [NAME], ADOPTED ON [DATE]. 1. SHARE SUBSCRIPTION: The board records the subscription of the entire stated share capital, set at [amount], divided into [number] ordinary shares of [par value] each, fully subscribed by the founding shareholders and paid in cash; the capital deposit certificate from [bank] is accepted and the funds remain blocked at the company’s disposal after registration. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office is fixed at [full address], France; the manager is authorized to sign the lease and to notify the Commercial Registry. 3. OFFICERS: [Name] is appointed corporate manager (gérant) and shall represent the company in all acts, including the licensing application before the AMF. All related documents and filings are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft Articles of Association and Open Blocked Capital Escrow Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (where required) or bank holding the deposit; BNP Paribas, Société Générale, Crédit Agricole, or any French bank account holding institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the French-language statuts signed by all shareholders, designate the gérant, specify the corporate object, registered office, share capital, and duration. Open a temporary blocked account in the company’s name at a French bank or before a notary and deposit the cash share capital. Obtain the capital deposit certificate (
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association
Shareholders' identity documents and proof of address
Bank or notary capital deposit certificate
Declaration of lawful funds of each subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open the account or the deposit certificate is rejected, deposit funds with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations or before a notary, obtain the substituted certificate, and resubmit the corrected dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the Statutory Notice of Formation in a Legal Announcement Journal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) authorized in the judicial department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Place a formal legal announcement containing the corporate name, form, share capital, registered office, corporate object, duration, and identity of managers. The publication must occur before or on the same day as the RCS filing and produce a certificate of publication.
required_dossiers: Draft of the legal announcement
Project of the articles of association
Certificate of appointment of the gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the journal returns the notice as incomplete, correct the announcement text and republish immediately; the cost and delay remain with the company unless the reporter made the error.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the Complete Incorporation Dossier to the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI – Guichet des formalités des entreprises; transmitted electronically to the Greffe du tribunal de commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online form at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, upload the signed statuts, legal announcement proof, capital-deposit certificate, declarations of beneficial owners and managers, and proof of office occupancy. Pay the applicable registry fee. The guichet transmits the dossier to the greffe; after approval the company receives its RCS number and SIREN/SIRET identifiers.
required_dossiers: Signed articles of association
Capital deposit certificate or notary attestation
Legal announcement certificate
Declaration of beneficial owners (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
Manager's declaration of conformity and non-conviction
Proof of authority to use the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the greffe issues a query, cure the irregularity within the prescribed deadline (generally 15 days) by filing the corrected document electronically; contest any final refusal before the judge appointed to supervise the commercial registry (juge commis à la surveillance du registre).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Official Registration Identifiers and Complete Post-Filing Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INSEE, URSSAF, DGFiP, and the Greffe du tribunal de commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, retrieve the extrait Kbis, verify the automatic assignment of SIREN, SIRET, and APE code corresponding to ISIC 6499/NAICS 523999, and confirm social-security and tax registration transmitted by the Guichet Unique. Open the company’s final commercial bank account and provide the Kbis to the bank for release of the blocked capital.
required_dossiers: Extrait Kbis
SIREN/SIRET notification from INSEE
Guichet Unique registration summary
Final banking authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If late or missing identifier notices occur, address a request to INPI and directly to INSEE/URSSAF using the RCS number; any incorrect APE code may be corrected through the Greffe by filing a rectificative notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Hold the First Board Meeting and Adopt Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company management (gérant) and shareholders in general; lawyers/corporate secretary as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting after registration, formally adopt the pro-forma resolution, open the share register, and approve the management mandate. The gérant is vested with powers to apply for the AMF crowdfunding-service-provider license and to engage professional advisers, sign contracts, and make all regulatory filings.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first board meeting
Share register (registre des mouvements de titres)
Signed management mandate
Corporate power-of-attorney for regulatory filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the minutes contain omissions, cure by adopting a supplementary board resolution and, where required, submit it for ratification by the shareholders at the next ordinary general meeting.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autorité des Marchés Financiers (AMF) in cooperation with the ACPR (Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority) for anti-money-laundering checks; cross-border notification under Regulation (EU) 2020/1503
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: European Crowdfunding Service Provider (ECSP) licence / Autorisation d'exercer comme Prestataire de Services de Financement Participatif (PSFP)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique and Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – pure digital intermediary with no physical manufacturing, industrial facility, or polluting installation; no environmental-impact assessment required under Article R.122-2 of the Code de l'environnement.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for industrial wastewater, VOC, or hazardous-waste discharge. The registered office must comply with general environmental hygiene and waste-sorting rules; any electronic equipment waste must be handled in accordance with Directive 2012/19/EU (WEEE), and cloud/data-centre subcontractors must observe European energy-efficiency and data-protection standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The registered office must satisfy French building, fire-safety, and disabled-access requirements applicable to commercial premises (Code de la construction et de l'habitation). No structural-load or workplace-atmosphere certificate is required for an office-only digital platform, but the company must maintain a health-and-safety register (registre de santé et de sécurité au travail), conduct an annual fire-safety review, and ensure the premises are covered by the employer's occupational-health declaration to the DREETS labour inspectorate.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — impots.gouv.fr; business portal 'Mon espace professionnel' dedicated to corporate and VAT declarations
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French-established SARL: incorporate via the Guichet unique/CFE using Form M0; DGFiP subsequently assigns a SIREN (9-digit) and SIRET (14-digit), and if the SARL executes taxable supplies the SIE (Service des Impôts des Entreprises) attributes an intra-Community VAT number (FR + key + SIREN) under CGI Art. 286 ter. For foreign entities not established in France but making taxable supplies, mandatory registration is effected through the Mini-Guichet étranger procedure under CGI Art. 286 quater; the non-resident VAT application is filed with the local SIE competent for non-residents or via the online demat portal. There is no separate statutory TIN apart from the SIREN/VAT number for corporate taxpayers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (impôt sur les sociétés at 25% standard rate; reduced 15% for eligible SMEs on the first €42,500 of taxable income); Territorial_Scope: France (worldwide taxation for French-resident SARL with foreign tax credit relief under tax treaties); Tax_Exempt_Zone: No special territorial exemptions are applicable to equity crowdfunding platform activity, whether in mainland France or otherwise.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No general check-the-box regime exists in France. Statutory elections available to a SARL include: (i) the option under CGI Art. 239 AA to be taxed as a partnership (régime translucide) where all shareholders are natural persons within a same family; (ii) the election under CGI Art. 223 A for fiscal consolidation (intégration fiscale) if the SARL holds more than 95% of French subsidiaries; (iii) for a real-estate or financial holding context, an option under CGI Art. 206-5 for certain co-ownership structures. Hybrid mismatch elections are not elective: the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) and French domestic provisions apply mandatory, non-elective disallowance and non-deduction rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Domestic SARL established in France: €37,500 per annum for supplies of services and intellectual rights (CGI Art. 293 B micro-enterprise exemption threshold; the threshold is €85,000 for supplies of goods, with a reduced threshold of €34,400 for certain services). Foreign taxable persons without French establishment: no registration threshold—the first taxable act in France triggers compulsory registration, except under the OSS (One-Stop-Shop) regime where a non-zero threshold applies to EU-distance sales of goods and certain services supplied to non-taxable persons.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: E-invoicing reform (originally 2024, postponed by 2023 plan): mandatory B2B domestic e-invoicing begins 1 September 2026 for large and mid-size enterprises and 1 September 2027 for SMEs/micro-enterprises. Invoices must be structured (XML/EDI) and transmitted through a certified Plateforme de Dématérialisation Partenaire (PDP); data must flow to the Portail Public de Facturation (PF) of DGFiP for exchange and audit. There is no real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping regime in France; the DGFiP performs post-issuance analytics. B2B transactions with non-EU customers remain subject to French e-reporting or in-scope invoicing rules. Equity crowdfunding portals must additionally maintain AMF-mandated investor transaction statements, but these are not fiscal clearing instruments.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods exported from the EU, French VAT is zero-rated under CGI Art. 262-II-1° where the goods are physically dispatched or transported outside the EU by or on behalf of the supplier and proof of export is produced within the statutory time limit. For services, zero-rating applies only where the place of supply is outside France under the B2B rule (customer established outside France/EU) or, for e-services to non-EU private consumers, where the effective use and enjoyment is outside the EU. The equity crowdfunding portal's qualitative services (listing fees, due diligence, advisory) to non-EU issuers may consequently be outside French VAT; to reinvest EU input VAT, the non-resident portal operator must file a VAT refund application under the EU 13th Directive or the French refund mechanism before the 30 September of the following year.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Uniform Customs Export Declaration (DAU) with movement reference number
Transport document proving physical exit from the EU: Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR
Inward remittance certificate / documentary evidence of payment from the non-EU counterparty
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The French tax and customs authorities rigorously audit export zero-rating claims; absence of compliant documentation within any 3-year verification window leads to retroactive VAT assessment (claw-back) plus collection of interest. Penalties range from 25% for minor errors to 40% for deliberate inaccuracy, and 80% for manoeuvres frauduleuses; criminal sanctions include imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to €50,000 (CGI Art. 1741). Repeated violations can lead to a permanent loss of the export exemption and, for crowdfunding portals, additional AMF disciplinary sanctions, including fines and withdrawal of the crowdfunding license. The 180-day inward remittance deadline, where contractually imposed by the underlying investment agreement, is not a French statutory FX deadline but is applied as a prudential control by the financial regulator in verifying cross-border crowdfunding round closings.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), with prudential and AML supervision delegated to the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR); the French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor) jointly administers cross-border capital surveillance under the Code Monétaire et Financier (CMF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both current and capital accounts, anchored in Articles 63-65 TFEU and CMF Articles L.151-1 et seq. No exchange-control authorization is required for foreign direct investment, equity injections, dividend remittances, or crowdfunding flows. Statutory reporting to Banque de France applies to cross-border payments and balance-of-payments statistics (monthly direct-investment declarations per Banque de France Notice No 2021-05; thresholds: transactions >= EUR 50,000 for trade/payments and direct-investment flows). Dividend repatriation from the SARL is unrestricted once the statutory solvency test is met (Code de Commerce Art. L.232-11), subject to the 25% domestic withholding tax reduced under the applicable double-tax treaty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. France is a Eurosystem member; export receipts may be kept in euros or foreign currency indefinitely with no mandatory surrender or conversion ratio. Reporting obligations only: export payments and receivables exceeding EUR 50,000 must be declared for balance-of-payments statistics to Banque de France by the resident exporter; there is no legal timeline for conversion.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: LOW for statutory client-fund segregation. Under Regulation (EU) 2020/1503 (Articles 10-11), client monies of a crowdfunding service provider must be held at a credit institution, an eligible payment institution, or an investment firm, with strict segregation and a prohibition on reuse. Non-EU offshore digital EMIs (e.g., US/UK neobanks) cannot serve this statutory function. Feasibility: MODERATE for ancillary operational-expense accounts with EU-licensed EMIs (Qonto, Treezor, or Sella/Soledair), which are acceptable for payroll/vendor payments but never for investor escrow.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French AML law (Code Monétaire et Financier Art. L.561-5; ACPR Position 2020-10) permits remote video identification of natural-person clients. For a PSFP-licensed SARL classified as high-risk, Tier-1 banks typically require a live video-interview with the managing director (gérant) and all UBOs, plus apostilled corporate documents. In practice: EU-resident UBOs can complete the full onboarding remotely; non-EU UBOs are often asked to attend one physical branch meeting in France or to engage an ACPR-accredited third-party KYC provider. Physical presence is not an absolute legal mandate but a de facto bank policy prerequisite for the PSFP sector.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PSFP / equity-crowdfunding license triggers high-risk classification under ACPR sectoral risk guidance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AMF/ACPR registration certificate for the PSFP, audited business plan, internal AML/CFT procedures and transaction-monitoring rules, client-funds segregation policy, statutory auditor's report on internal controls (Règlement (UE) 2020/1503).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or non-EU UBOs and possible PEP exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passport and residence proof for each UBO, Source-of-Wealth and Source-of-Funds statements, negative-media and PEP screening reports, tax-residency certificates, and a PEP declaration with enhanced due-diligence file.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large-volume, low-ticket inbound investor payments creating unusual transaction velocity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Algorithmic AML monitoring documentation, investor on-boarding KYC process (identity verification), transaction velocity limits, escrow-flow diagram, and independent audit confirmation that client funds are isolated from the portal's own treasury.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-country exposure or sanctions-related geographic flags in the investor base
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening tooling (EU/UN/OFAC), jurisdiction risk matrix, investor prohibition policy, and correspondence-banking records supporting the country-risk assessment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for an equity injection into the French SARL: SEPA Credit Transfer (euros) or SWIFT MT103 (non-EEA currency) quoting the BOP purpose code for direct investment - French balance-of-payments code 'Investissement direct - Apports en capital' (BPM6 direct-investment equity category). Supporting documents for the receiving French bank: extraordinary general meeting resolution approving the capital increase, updated share register, attestation of contribution release, and UBO declarations; the bank files the mandatory Banque de France monthly direct-investment declaration. For third-country wire transfers, include full remittance data (shareholder name, nature 'Capital Increase', beneficiary SARL name and SIREN) to avoid classification as a loan or re-invoicing flow.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for disbursements by the crowdfunding portal: SEPA Credit Transfer for EU/EEA euro payments and SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA transfers; each project company receives funds through a segregated sub-account, with remittance information carrying the deal code, portfolio company identifiers, and the governing funding agreement reference. For larger structured disbursements or equipment financing underlying the crowd-funded transactions, Commercial Letters of Credit (documentary credits, UCP 600) may be issued by the portal's bank, although for pure equity-crowdfunding outflows the standard rail is a plain CT/MT103 with the correct purpose code 'D.2 - Capital transfer / direct investment'.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forwards (Change à terme) - available with any ACPR-licensed credit institution for hedging balance-sheet and operational exposures in currencies such as USD/GBP; no regulatory restriction for non-financial corporates.
Cross-Currency Swaps (Swap de change) - permitted for matching long-term investment or financing flows; require a board-approved treasury policy and ISDA/CMF master agreement.

Purchased FX Options (Option de change) - permissible for hedging; the writing (selling) of options is considered speculative for non-financial entities and is not recommended without bank authorization.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDF) - not practically available for EUR pairs (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF) because the euro is fully convertible and trades on a deliverable interbank basis; NDFs are limited to exotic non-convertible emerging-market currency legs.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts at the annual ordinary general meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company records; minutes entered in the SARL decisions register at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the financial year end; for a calendar-year SARL, by the last day of June; court order may extend this deadline only in exceptional cases
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the meeting may expose the manager to shareholder claims and prevent valid filing of the annual accounts; persistent failure may lead to judicial dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts and statutory audit report with the commercial registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the INPI Guichet unique; RCS dossier
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of shareholder approval; for a calendar-year SARL, no later than 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The court may impose a coercive fine on the company; continued non-filing leads to the registry flagging the company as non-compliant and can trigger administrative strike-off or judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return form 2065 with annexes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Second working day after 1 May for a calendar-year taxpayer; for a different accounting year, within three months after the year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10%, increased to 40% after formal notice; late-payment interest accrues monthly; tax enforcement measures may be commenced but administrative strike-off is not the direct consequence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Verification of the beneficial owner declaration and filing of any change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés through the statutory formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership; annual confirmation of the UBO position is a management duty at the annual general meeting, with no separate national annual UBO declaration form
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of up to EUR 5,000 for an individual and EUR 25,000 for a legal entity for non-filing or inaccurate filing; inaccurate UBO information may also block other registry filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual regulatory compliance report for the licensed equity crowdfunding portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within the deadline stated in the AMF authorisation decision, commonly aligned with the annual accounts approval and filing period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AMF enforcement measures may include pecuniary sanctions, suspension or withdrawal of the crowdfunding authorisation, and public warnings; no direct RCS strike-off is triggered by AMF sanctions alone.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is mandatory for a SARL when it exceeds at least two of the following thresholds at the balance sheet date for the last two consecutive financial years: EUR 4,000,000 balance sheet total, EUR 8,000,000 net turnover excluding VAT, and 50 average employees. A licensed equity crowdfunding portal may also be required to appoint an independent auditor as a condition of its AMF authorisation or as a regulated financial intermediary.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP, comprising the Plan Comptable General and ANC Regulation No. 2014-03, governs the SARL's individual statutory accounts. IFRS is not permitted for the standalone statutory financial statements of a French SARL; it is relevant only where consolidated accounts are prepared in accordance with French commercial law.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must maintain a current record of beneficial owners, defined as any natural person directly or indirectly holding more than 25% of capital or voting rights or otherwise exercising control. At each annual ordinary general meeting the manager must review the UBO position, confirm its accuracy, and file any change with the RCS within 30 days. This annual confirmation is a governance control and should be documented in the management report; it does not create a separate annual UBO filing in France.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of members and share transfer register
Minutes register of shareholders' and managers' decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $600 to $1,800 per year for a professional registered office and corporate secretarial service in France, depending on city and scope
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $7,000 to $22,000 per year for the independent statutory audit of a small-to-medium French SARL operating as a regulated equity crowdfunding portal

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) at 25% for fiscal years commencing after 1 January 2022. A reduced rate of 15% applies to the first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs with annual turnover below EUR 10 million, fully paid-up capital, and at least 75% ownership held by individuals or qualifying fellow SMEs. France does not grant a sector-specific tax holiday for equity crowdfunding portals; however, qualifying research and innovation expenditures may generate the Crédit d'Impôt Recherche (CIR) and Crédit d'Impôt Innovation (CII), which reduce effective tax cost.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: French liasse fiscale consisting of Form 2065-SD / 2065 (déclaration de résultats) and annexes 2050 to 2059-G. Mandatory filing is effected electronically through impots.gouv.fr (EFI/EDI) or a certified tax filing intermediary.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing with four quarterly corporate income tax instalments during the fiscal year and one final balance settlement at the filing deadline.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal years ending 31 December, the return must be filed by the second working day after 1 May of the following year. For fiscal years ending on any other date, the return must be filed within three months of the fiscal year-end. Instalment payment dates under the standard calendar are 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December, with the balance due at the same time as the annual return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal form, corporate name, SIREN/SIRET, registered office, primary NAF/APE activity code, and fiscal year closing date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only the French SARL's identifying data. The non-resident shareholder is not entered on the headline identification fields; share ownership details appear in the mandates or special annexes where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net income before tax adjusted for non-deductible expenses, fiscal depreciation, provisions, tax credits, and loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only profit attributable to the French permanent establishment or French corporate operations. Foreign parent income, group losses, or foreign branch losses must not be aggregated into the French return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses of prior years carried forward and applied against current-year taxable profits, with the remaining loss carryforward pool shown.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses sustained by a foreign parent or non-resident affiliate cannot be transferred to the French SARL unless the same French taxpayer validly incurred the loss under French tax rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of corporate income tax on taxable profit at 25% or 15% where eligible, net of tax credits and previously paid instalments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The French entity is solely liable for the tax reported on this line. A foreign parent may not offset its own taxes or pre-paid profits against the French CIT liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an automatic 10% surcharge on net CIT due plus late-payment interest of 0.20% per month. A formal notice may raise the surcharge if no response is given. Deliberate understatement attracts a 40% penalty; fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of law attract an 80% penalty. Criminal tax fraud may result in imprisonment of up to five years and fines of up to EUR 75,000 under Article 1741 of the French General Tax Code.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The 25% domestic French withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders may be reduced or eliminated under an applicable double tax treaty or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive. To obtain relief, the recipient must provide a valid tax residence certificate (attestation de résidence fiscale) using the Cerfa 5000-series or a Form 6166 certificate for certain treaty partners. For source-country relief before payment, the non-resident recipient must submit Form 5000/5001 self-certification to the French paying company, confirming beneficial ownership and treaty entitlement. If the domestic rate was withheld, refund relief may be claimed from the French tax administration within the applicable statute of limitations. Relief is not automatic; the French payer must verify that the recipient has economic substance, is not a conduit, and meets the relevant ownership holding period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic French withholding on royalties paid to non-residents is generally 33.33% under source rules, while interest may be subject to 12.8% withholding in specific debt-instrument cases. Under standard French tax treaties, royalty withholding is commonly reduced to 5% and interest to 0%. Under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive, interest and royalty payments made by a French company to a qualifying associated EU company may be wholly exempt from French withholding. Equity crowdfunding platform commissions are normally characterised as service income rather than royalties, so the transactional nature must be analysed against the relevant treaty before applying a reduced rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 (annual turnover or total balance-sheet assets of the French entity or consolidated group triggering formal Local File and Master File obligations under Article 223 quinquies C of the French General Tax Code). A smaller French SARL remains required to maintain contemporaneous arm's length documentation whenever it enters material cross-border transactions with related parties, particularly service fees paid to foreign fintech or platform affiliates.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply Cayman-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR). The functional equivalent is the French abuse-of-law doctrine under Article L64 of the French Book of Tax Procedure, ATAD anti-hybrid and CFC rules, permanent establishment thresholds, and the OECD BEPS minimum standard. For an equity crowdfunding portal, real operational substance requires an AMF or ECSPR regulatory licence, local employees and decision-making, authentic escrow and client-asset controls, robust AML/KYC procedures, and contemporaneous records demonstrating commercial activity. Failure to demonstrate substance may result in recharacterisation as a shell or conduit, denial of treaty benefits, and joint liability of the gérant.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating crowdfunding platform commissions, concealing fee revenue through foreign payment processors, booking investor escrow flows as taxable turnover, or filing false corporate income tax returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of 40% for intentional misstatement and 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of law, plus late-payment interest at 0.20% per month. Criminal liability under Article 1741 of the French General Tax Code exposes the taxpayer to imprisonment of up to five years and fines up to EUR 75,000, with additional court-ordered publication and forfeiture sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SARL gérant or de facto director may be jointly and severally liable for penalties caused by intentional fault. A criminal conviction can trigger asset seizure, travel restrictions, disqualification from managing companies, and civil restitution to the tax administration and investors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an equity crowdfunding portal without AMF approval or European Crowdfunding Service Provider (ECSPR) authorisation, facilitating securities offerings above regulatory thresholds, or failing to comply with prospectus rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AMF administrative injunctions and fines, regulatory licence revocation, and criminal sanctions under the French Monetary and Financial Code for unlawful financial intermediation. Penalties may include fines of up to EUR 100 million or statutory ceilings based on unlawful proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managers can be held civilly liable for investor losses, barred from managing regulated financial entities, subjected to AMF fines, and in serious cases face criminal imprisonment and travel bans during investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abuse of Law and Fictitious Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a nominal French SARL with no real operational activity, local personnel, or decision-making, used solely to route crowdfunding fees or profits to a foreign parent or to claim treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterisation as an abusive arrangement under Article L64 LPF with an 80% penalty, denial of treaty and EU directive benefits, reassessment of profits to the French taxpayer, and retroactive tax collection with late-payment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced where the legal form conceals the true principal or is used abusively. The gérant can be jointly liable for tax liabilities, subject to civil restitution to misled investors, and may face disqualification, asset freezes, and criminal sanctions for fictitious operations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying inflated management, technology, software, marketing, or data-processing fees to a non-resident affiliate, or receiving under-priced platform services, in order to shift taxable profit outside France.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Arm's length price adjustment reallocating profits to the French SARL, disallowance of excessive deductions, a 40% penalty for deliberate mispricing, and additional transfer pricing documentation penalties where local/master file obligations are not satisfied. Failing to provide documentation on request may also trigger formal assessment procedures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant may be jointly and severally liable for penalties resulting from fraudulent or abusive arrangement, and may face criminal charges for tax evasion where fictitious service fees are documented. Civil liability extends to reimbursement of falsely deducted sums and compensation to minority shareholders or investors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Money Laundering Through Escrow and Crowdfunding Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting investor funds without customer due diligence, ignoring suspicious transaction reports, failing to verify beneficial ownership of invested vehicles, or allowing the platform to be used for money laundering and sanctions evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Sanctions under the French Monetary and Financial Code and AML regulator decisions, including fines, licence suspension or withdrawal, closure orders, and criminal prosecution for money laundering. Money laundering offences carry heavy criminal fines and imprisonment up to ten years in aggravated cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and AML compliance officers face personal criminal liability for deliberate non-reporting or complicity in laundering. Courts may order asset confiscation, travel bans, professional disqualification, and civil damages to defrauded investors and regulatory authorities.
